attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as an 802.1Q trunk router on eth1 with sub-interfaces eth1.10 (VLAN10, 10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (VLAN20, 10.10.20.1/24), each in its own firewall zone with forward=REJECT and no inter-zone forwarding rule. node2's ens7 got VLAN10 sub-interface ens7.10 (10.10.10.2/24) and node3's ens7 got VLAN20 sub-interface ens7.20 (10.10.20.2/24), both persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/vlan.cfg with the vlan kernel module in /etc/modules. Verified node2 and node3 each reach node1 on their own VLAN, while forwarded traffic between the two VLANs is actively refused (ICMP Destination Port Unreachable from node1) rather than merely dropped. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot/shutdown -r), boot_id changes were captured proving genuine restarts, and post-restart checks confirmed the VLAN interfaces, firewall zones, and cross-VLAN isolation all survived and function identically after reboot.
